<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917498_theRebbe_163" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917498_theRebbe_163__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the perfection of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) is when it permeates all particular powers and the service of every individual throughout the entire year, thereby causing the "sleep of the King of the world to be disturbed" and drawing down the transcendent light into the source of time and even into the chronicles of the days.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be understood in more particularity based on what is known, that the perfection of mesiras nefesh is when the mesiras nefesh</t>
    <t s="1">(which stems from the Yechidah)</t>
    <t s="2">is drawn and also acts within the particular powers,</t>
    <t s="3">"with all your heart and with all your soul"—that even the particular service of each and every power should be in a manner of mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="4">above measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="5">And the mesiras nefesh was present among all of Israel,</t>
    <t s="6">from youth to elder, infants and women,</t>
    <t s="7">and it can be said that the intention in this is</t>
    <t s="8">that even the particular service of each individual</t>
    <t s="9">(youth,</t>
    <t s="10">elder,</t>
    <t s="11">infants and women)</t>
    <t s="12">was permeated with the movement of mesiras nefesh.</t>
    <t s="13">And it can be said that this is another aspect in what is written in the maamar, that their mesiras nefesh was throughout the entire year,</t>
    <t s="14">for during the year there are all the changes of the seasons</t>
    <t s="15">[and as is explained in several discourses</t>
    <t s="16">regarding the quality of the esrog</t>
    <t s="17">(for the esrog is the aspect of Malchus,</t>
    <t s="18">its concept being that of Esther)</t>
    <t s="19">that it dwells on its tree from year to year],</t>
    <t s="20">and in every season there is a particular service,</t>
    <t s="21">and even in every day</t>
    <t s="22">(within that same season itself)</t>
    <t s="23">there is a particular service that belongs to that day,</t>
    <t s="24">as the saying,</t>
    <t s="25">"Each and every day performs its task,"</t>
    <t s="26">and that they stood in mesiras nefesh all year,</t>
    <t s="27">perhaps another intention can be said in this,</t>
    <t s="28">that even the matters of the year</t>
    <t s="29">(the particular service of each and every day)</t>
    <t s="30">were in a manner of mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="31">above measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="32">And this is that the matter of "the sleep of the King of the world was disturbed" is brought about specifically by their standing in mesiras nefesh all year,</t>
    <t s="33">for through their mesiras nefesh shining in revelation also within the particular powers</t>
    <t s="34">(all year),</t>
    <t s="35">through this it is likewise so above,</t>
    <t s="36">that the light that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="37">"the sleep of the King was disturbed,"</t>
    <t s="38">is drawn down in a manner of pnimiyus (inwardness),</t>
    <t s="39">and even to "He said to bring the book of records, the chronicles of the days,"</t>
    <t s="40">that it is drawn also into the book of records, the chronicles of the days,</t>
    <t s="41">the root of time</t>
    <t s="42">(as explained in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="43">and even to "and it was found written, etc."</t>
    <t s="44">also in the book of records of Shushan the capital in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="45">even in the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="46">"they were exiled to Eilam"</t>
    <t s="47">(Shushan)</t>
    <t s="48">"the Shechinah is with them."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that just as in the exile of Eilam, so too in every exile the Shechinah is with Israel, and through the service of mesiras nefesh that permeates all particular matters of Torah and mitzvos, the "sleep of the King is disturbed," drawing down the transcendent light into the source of time and even into the simple reality of the exile, culminating in the transformation of darkness to light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And just as it was in the exile of Eilam,</t>
    <t s="2">so too is it in every exile,</t>
    <t s="3">that in every place where Israel were exiled, the Shechinah is with them,</t>
    <t s="4">and they were exiled to Edom, the Shechinah is with them.</t>
    <t s="5">For through Israel standing in mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="6">that they are not ashamed before the mockers,</t>
    <t s="7">which is connected to the movement of mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="8">and the movement of mesiras nefesh of "let him not be ashamed before the mockers" is drawn within him in the particular matters of Torah and mitzvos throughout the entire day,</t>
    <t s="9">for this is that this matter</t>
    <t s="10">("let him not be ashamed before the mockers")</t>
    <t s="11">is the beginning of all four sections of the Shulchan Aruch,</t>
    <t s="12">and even that the movement of mesiras nefesh brings him also to increase in the study of Torah and in beautification in the fulfillment of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="13">and even that the increase is above measure, since it comes from the aspect of mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="14">and even that it is recognizable in his study of Torah and fulfillment of mitzvos that they are done with mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="15">and all the more so with awe and love,</t>
    <t s="16">that in his study of Torah he remembers the Giver of the Torah</t>
    <t s="17">and his fulfillment of mitzvos is permeated with the feeling of the Commander of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="18">"Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"</t>
    <t s="19">and as is explained at length in the discourses of the Mitteler Rebbe</t>
    <t s="20">that in all the mitzvos there must be the general intention</t>
    <t s="21">(which is equal in all the mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="22">that he fulfills the command of the King of the world.</t>
    <t s="23">And through the service of mesiras nefesh,</t>
    <t s="24">and particularly that the mesiras nefesh is drawn and acts within the particular matters of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="25">behold, through this "the sleep of the King is disturbed,"</t>
    <t s="26">that the light above the chain of descent is drawn down even into the book of records, the chronicles of the days,</t>
    <t s="27">the root of time and time,</t>
    <t s="28">and even to "and they shall be called before the king,"</t>
    <t s="29">also before King Achashverosh in its simple sense in this physical world, while we are still "servants of Achashverosh,"</t>
    <t s="30">that even when they are still in the time of exile and "the law of the kingdom is law"</t>
    <t s="31">(and Mordechai is only the viceroy),</t>
    <t s="32">nevertheless then "and they shall be"</t>
    <t s="33">"kings your nursemaids,"</t>
    <t s="34">and they decree upon those who were initially opponents of the Jews and Judaism that they should assist the Jews and Judaism,</t>
    <t s="35">and even that "darkness is transformed into light and bitterness into sweetness,"</t>
    <t s="36">similar to what was in the days of Mordechai and Esther,</t>
    <t s="37">that King Achashverosh decreed upon the opponent that he should go and proclaim before Mordechai the Jew, "Thus shall be done to the man whom the king desires to honor,"</t>
    <t s="38">the King of the world, and also, with the appropriate distinction, etc., King Achashverosh in its simple sense.</t>
    <t s="39">And even to "for the Jews there was light and joy and gladness and honor"</t>
    <t s="40">and so may it be for us,</t>
    <t s="41">"light"</t>
    <t s="42">this is Torah</t>
    <t s="43">[and in Torah itself,</t>
    <t s="44">"light" is a feminine term, referring to the Oral Torah,</t>
    <t s="45">Torah in its explanation,</t>
    <t s="46">from which light goes out to the entire world]</t>
    <t s="47">and "joy" this is a festival, and "gladness" this is circumcision, and "honor" these are tefillin,</t>
    <t s="48">for the entire Torah is compared to tefillin,</t>
    <t s="49">and it can be said that it also includes the tefillin of the Master of the world, about which it is written "and who"</t>
    <t s="50">"is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land,"</t>
    <t s="51">meaning that the superiority of Israel is revealed in a revealed way,</t>
    <t s="52">"the sleep of the King was disturbed."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section concludes that from the redemption of Purim, which occurs in the final moments of exile, we immediately proceed to the true and complete redemption, where all Jews will be redeemed with the completeness of the people, Torah, and land, in a manner of alacrity beyond all measure.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And from the juxtaposition of redemption to redemption,</t>
    <t s="2">that from this redemption of "for the Jews there was light and joy and gladness and honor" at the time when they are still in the final moments of exile,</t>
    <t s="3">they will come immediately in juxtaposition to the true and complete redemption,</t>
    <t s="4">that "kings your nursemaids will bring the children of Israel" just as "the children of Israel bring the offering in a pure vessel"</t>
    <t s="5">to the Holy Land,</t>
    <t s="6">"a land which... the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year,"</t>
    <t s="7">and there itself, in Jerusalem, the city of the great King,</t>
    <t s="8">Dovid, the King Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="9">and there itself, on the holy mountain,</t>
    <t s="10">and in the Sanctuary, "O L-rd, Your hands have established."</t>
    <t s="11">And all this will be in a manner of alacrity,</t>
    <t s="12">and even to alacrity in the ultimate, above all measure and limitation, and even in a manner</t>
    <t s="13">(of "until")</t>
    <t s="14">of "does not know,"</t>
    <t s="15">that one dances in with great joy, above all measure and limitation, into the true and complete redemption, speedily in our days, literally.</t>
    <t s="16">All the Jews throughout all the generations,</t>
    <t s="17">and at their head the Nasi of our generation, etc., and Mordechai the Jew and Esther the queen,</t>
    <t s="18">all of them will be redeemed from the exile—the completeness of the redemption,</t>
    <t s="19">together with the completeness of the people and the completeness of the Torah and the completeness of the land,</t>
    <t s="20">and in a manner of "the L-rd your G-d will expand your border,"</t>
    <t s="21">also the land of the Kenite, Kenizite, and Kadmonite,</t>
    <t s="22">and a verse does not depart from its simple meaning,</t>
    <t s="23">and on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="24">the world of the simple meaning, which is</t>
    <t s="25">this lowly physical world and the world of action—it is the main thing and the foundation upon which the entire order of the chain of descent stands,</t>
    <t s="26">as per the well-known explanation of "and behold, the L-rd stands upon it."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
